meta.title: Hungarian C1 Advanced
meta.subtitle: 1500 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Hungarian → English (see the Hungarian, recall the meaning) and English → Hungarian (see an English meaning, recall the Hungarian). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1500 words of Hungarian for an advanced learner, aligned to C1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts, and recognise implicit meaning' — a learner here is able to express ideas fluently and spontaneously without much obvious searching for expressions, to use language flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes, and to produce clear, well-structured, detailed text on complex subjects. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: Hungarian has examinations at these levels, but no graded word list for any of them was found published, so this deck is not an examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 313 of the 1500 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — philosophy and ethics, religion and the inner life, scholarly Hungarian, government, diplomacy and the constitution, the economy and development, medicine and the body, law and rights, language and literature, the shades of feeling and judgement, the abstract nouns and adjectives of formal prose, and the literary connectors and adverbs — and the other 1187 are the commonest remaining words of everyday Hungarian, taken from a frequency list built from film and television subtitles and counted by the WHOLE word, every case of a noun and every form of a verb added together. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Verbs are given as Hungarian dictionaries give them, in the third person singular (eszik "eats", lát "sees"), the form the endings are built on. The 698 nouns show their plural, their accusative and their "his, her" form, the part vowel harmony makes hard to guess (ló, lovak, lovat, lova), and behind the All forms fold every case in both numbers; the 317 verbs show their "I" form, their past and their infinitive (eszik, eszem, evett, enni), and behind the fold the present in both conjugations — the definite one is used when the object is definite (látok egy házat, "I see a house"; látom a házat, "I see the house") — the past, the conditional and the imperative by person. The Hungarian Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the letters and their sounds. Real example sentences come with 1350 of the 1500 words, three apiece for 1102 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings and forms: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.

A freegánok ezt az elképzelést egy lépéssel továbbviszik, felismerve, hogy egy komplex, ipari, tömegtermeléssel működő és profitvezérelt gazdaságban az emberek, az állatok és a Föld bántalmazása a termelés minden szintjén jellemző (a nyersanyagok beszerzésétől a termelésen keresztül egészen a szállításig), és gyakorlatilag minden termékkel együtt jár, amit csak vásárolni szoktunk.
Vegans are people who avoid products from animal sources or products tested on animals in an effort to avoid harming animals. Freegans take this a step further by recognizing that in a complex, industrial, mass-production economy driven by profit, abuses of humans, animals, and the earth abound at all levels of production (from acquisition to raw materials to production to transportation) and in just about every product we buy.
